title: Development Of Combat Techniques
paragraphs: “They’ve also developed airships and airplanes, and they even own tanks.”
“They’re that advanced? I thought they only had steam engines in the game…”
“That’s another way this world differs from the game.”
“Seems like it. The place is a popular base, but it’s so big…”
“In online games, would it be considered the capital?”
“It’s definitely the starting capital. But after they implemented higher living costs, it started to decline.”
“Ah… yeah, that happens. Places that get abandoned due to some mysterious update. In a game I played, the layout of a city changed, and people stopped gathering there.”
Ren and Itsuki seem to have gotten quite used to traveling by carriage. Though, they still get motion sickness from time to time. It’s best not to rely too much on medicine to suppress the symptoms.
“It sounds like representatives from various nations are staying there too, so it might be difficult to exploit the Heroes.”
“That makes sense. And as for the Waves, we won’t have to deal with them until we arrive?”
“We’re supposed to be summoned for the Waves in Melromarc, right?”
“There are still over three weeks left. As long as we reach Faubrey and register at their Dragon Hourglass, we’ll be fine.”

With that, the discussion was settled. A journey by carriage—there’s something peaceful about it. And so, several days passed as Yuki and the others pulled the carriage. Along the way, we stopped by regions inhabited by monsters to gather materials and level up. Father and the others are growing stronger at a steady pace.
“For the most part, we’ve learned all the known strengthening methods.”
In the evening, as Father skillfully prepared a meal, Ren spoke to me.
“Yeah. To be honest, most of the monsters we encounter can’t even hurt me, so they just ignore me.”
“Indeed, Iwatani-dono possesses an unnaturally high level of defense. I feel the same way.”
“That’s why I focus on restraining them or using skills to protect others.”
“Sakura worked hard!”
“Yeah, it’s all thanks to you, Sakura-chan. And Éclair, too.”
“Recently, I’ve started feeling like I lack strength. After hunting with Amaki-dono and Kawasumi-dono, I really felt it.”

While saying this, Éclair was sparring with Ren. Ren had switched his sword to a low-attack wooden blade to train with her. Every so often, Éclair managed to land a strike on him. Well, Ren is still inexperienced. It becomes painfully obvious whenever he spars with me.
“I still think I have the edge in technique…”
“Yeah… At first, I found it frustrating, but after losing to Motoyasu and Éclair so many times, I’ve just accepted it.”
“You kept insisting you never lost in the beginning, though.”

Whenever Ren was about to lose to me or Éclair, he would unleash a skill. Of course, both I, Itsuki, and Father warned him that running away just to avoid losing was not an option. Eventually, he gave up on that tactic.
“Shut up. Back in Brave Star Online, I was pretty confident.”
“You were one of the stronger players in the game?”
Oh? Ren turned his face away. Well, I suppose it’s a gamer’s pride. I understand that a little—my past self had a similar mindset.
“I was good at one-on-one duels.”
“Huh.”
“I even beat someone who was famous in another game.”
“…Another game?”
Father listened to Ren’s words and murmured curiously. Ren then started coughing repeatedly.
“Isn’t it that guy? The one who kind of resembles Naofumi-san. Naofumi-san, maybe it’s best if we don’t bring it up too much.”
“Ah… so he’s a rival because they know each other?”
“Don’t look at me with that pitying expression!”
Hahaha, Ren is as amusing as ever.
“In any case, I could never match Motoyasu-kun’s spear skills.”
“I have been in quite a few battles, after all.”

There are also the forceful attacks using skills, but considering the total time I’ve spent fighting due to the time loops, it’s been well over a year. Naturally, my body movements have improved. The training I did under Father’s guidance in the first world is definitely paying off.
“My current goal is to land a single hit on either Éclair or Motoyasu.”
“I’m envious. Neither Naofumi-san nor I can even manage one hit.”
“Yeah. In my case, I can’t even use joint locks, so at best, I can just grab or grapple.”

Itsuki only fights from a distance with his bow. The most he can do is work on his footwork, I suppose. And since Father focuses on blocking attacks, mastering his fighting style must be quite difficult.
“The future version of Father once said that, as a Shield Hero, deflecting an opponent’s impact is key to his fighting style.”
It seems that the previous Father naturally mastered it as well.
“Impact, huh… You mean like, for example, if Éclair were to thrust her sword, you intercept it before the full force comes out, deflect it, or even pull back to make her attack miss?”
“Precisely. That’s what I do as well.”
“Then, Iwatani-dono, watch closely. I shall attempt a thrust against Kitamura-dono.”
“Alright.”
“Amaki-dono, you should take note of this too.”
“I understand.”

I readied my spear and waited for Éclair to attack. She took a deep breath, placed her hand on her sword, and then quickly closed the distance with a strong forward movement. To keep things fair, I deliberately used a weaker spear against her. Due to the status enhancements, I could technically counter her easily, but even so, Éclair was quite fast. Reflexively, I deflected her thrust with the tip of my spear, narrowly dodged her follow-up counter, and stopped my spear’s shaft just short of touching her chest.
“Haa…”
Father let out a sound while cooking as he observed our exchange. Honestly, Ren and Itsuki should learn from him—being able to cook while watching something else is a skill in itself.
“This is how Kitamura-dono deflected my attack, then read my sword movements and dodged. As a result, I left an opening that he exploited.”
“I see.”
“…Hmph.”
Itsuki, who had been clapping, asked a question after watching the exchange.
“This seems like a good countermeasure against close-range attacks… but what should I do in my case?”
“Given the nature of the bow, Kawasumi-dono, you should focus on reading your opponent’s movements as a foundation.”
“I’ve never heard of a school of archery that focuses on melee combat… Should I just dodge like in a monster-hunting game?”
“You could also leave close-range combat to the front-line fighters.”
“Maybe the problem is that an archer getting forced into close combat is already a failure in itself.”
Well, in Itsuki’s case, using skills to escape would be the ideal option. From previous time loops, I know he has some close-range attacks, so it all depends on how he develops from here.
“Motoyasu-san, what did the future me do?”
“You left close combat to your allies.”
“That makes it sound like I didn’t train at all!”

Itsuki sounded like he felt left out. But he is the Bow Hero, after all. The whole point is for him to continuously attack from a distance. Ideally, he should become strong enough to defeat enemies before they even get close.
“Must be nice. Plus, with your special ability, your shots almost never miss, right? That’s basically a cheat that lets you stay strong without even training.”
“Ugh… Being left out because of my ability is humiliating.”
“I think being an archer who never hits allies and can fire at enemies with near-perfect accuracy is already incredible, though.”

“Yeah, exactly. That’s a valuable skill. Archers in organized armies typically focus on firing volleys like a rain of arrows, right? You’re doing that all on your own with skills, which is already impressive.”
“Alright, I’ll focus on strategies that prevent enemies from getting close.”
“I think that’s the right call for now. By the way, Itsuki, I feel like in your original world, robots from the future could totally show up.”
Lately, Father has been making comments like that about Itsuki more often. It’s probably because when we studied together, he noticed that Itsuki’s academic performance wasn’t great.
“Naofumi-san, please stop mocking me. You’re just analyzing me based on some manga or anime, aren’t you? But I’ve never had any experiences that bizarre.”
“I’m not mocking you… but your stories do make for entertaining bedtime reading.”
“Honestly, I think so too.”

Now that I think about it, Father and Ren often ask Itsuki questions at night. They seem particularly curious about what kind of incidents happened in his world with people who had supernatural abilities, or about the general plots of dramas and manga. For Itsuki, these things might be completely ordinary, but to us, they’re intriguing.
“My world is turning into entertainment for you guys!?”
“Stories about superpowered people dealing with supernatural crimes are pretty fun to hear, even secondhand.”
“That’s not fair! What about Ren-san and Naofumi-san’s worlds?”
“Honestly, being around all of you, who come from such weirdly different versions of Japan, makes me question my own Japan too…”

Father looked at Ren, Itsuki, and me in turn. Meanwhile, Sakura-chan and the others were eagerly waiting for Father’s cooking. As he efficiently plated the completed dishes, Ren, Itsuki, and even Éclair stared at him in mild disbelief.
“I don’t really have anything special about my world.”
“Maybe he’s from a cooking manga world.”
“That actually makes sense. If you analyse Naofumi’s thought process using a non-VR era perspective, some things don’t quite add up.”
“A cooking manga world…? There weren’t any weird culinary schools or anything. And I don’t remember reading about cooking duels in newspaper features, either…”
That’s an amusing way to put it. It’s probably just how slice-of-life anime depict everyday life. I used to hear about that kind of thing when I was on good terms with those so-called otaku.
But with that logic, wouldn’t practically anything fit the description?
“By the way, the previous Father described me as—”
For the record, I was not modeled after a hopeless loser.
